info.title: freehire API — internal reference
info.description:
## Base URL

All endpoints are served under `https://freehire.me/api/v1`. The API is read-first and open: the job, search, facet, and company endpoints need no authentication and may be called cross-origin.

Authenticated endpoints accept either the browser session cookie (set by sign-in, same-origin) or a personal API key sent as a Bearer token — see the authentication model below. Keys are created in your account, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys), not through this API.

## Response envelope

Single items are wrapped as `{ "data": ... }`. Collections add pagination metadata: `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "total", "limit", "offset" } }`. Errors are `{ "error": "message" }` with a matching HTTP status.

```json
{ "data": { "...": "single item" } }

{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "total": 4213, "limit": 20, "offset": 0 } }

{ "error": "job not found" }
```

## Pagination

List and search endpoints page with `limit` (default 20, max 100) and `offset` (default 0). `meta.total` reports the total matching the current filters, so you can compute the number of pages.

Pagination is bounded on **every** list endpoint: `offset + limit` may not exceed 10000 (`pagination too deep` → 400). This is deep-paging protection, not a cap on the reported total — use filters to narrow rather than paging that far.

The bound is a refusal rather than a clamp, deliberately: a clamped page would answer 200 carrying rows you did not ask for, and a client walking pages would loop over the same page forever without being able to tell. A 400 means "there is no such page", which is the truth.

## Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes: 400 (bad request / invalid value), 401 (missing or invalid credentials), 403 (authenticated but not allowed, e.g. a non-moderator), 404 (no such job, company, or owned resource), 429 (request limit exceeded), and 503 (service temporarily unavailable). Application errors use `{ "error": ... }`. nginx rate-limit rejections can return a non-JSON body; see API plans below.

## API plans

The public read endpoints answer without a key for personal and non-commercial use. Showing the postings in a product you offer to others needs an [API plan](https://freehire.me/jobs-api), under the [data licence](https://freehire.me/terms#data-licence).

Send a full-access key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or use the OAuth access token of a signed-in MCP or CLI connection.

The API plan allows 1,200 requests per 60-second window. The Data plan allows 6,000. Neither paid API plan has a daily request cap. The account shares one budget across its full-access API keys and OAuth connections, including public REST reads and agent search. A browser session cookie does not select the paid API rate.

The limit counts HTTP requests, not returned listings or unique vacancies. A page containing 100 listings costs one request. Re-fetching the same page or vacancy costs another request, including when the data has not changed. There is no separate cooldown for refreshing a vacancy.

Pagination returns 20 listings by default and up to 100 with `limit=100`. Requests carrying `offset` or `company_slug` also pass through separate per-IP nginx limits of 2 requests per second each, including paid requests. The `offset` limit allows a burst of 50 excess requests; the `company_slug` limit allows 30. A request carrying both parameters draws on both limits. For sustained pagination or company-filtered reads, keep the combined traffic from one IP within the applicable 2-request-per-second limit.

The gateway returns `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until reset). A window starts with its first request. Exceeding a request limit returns HTTP 429. Gateway rejections include `Retry-After` in seconds; nginx rejections can omit these headers and return a non-JSON body. Pause for `Retry-After` when present; otherwise back off before retrying.

## Authentication model

Browser clients authenticate with an `HttpOnly` session cookie set on sign-in (same-origin; the SPA cannot read it). Non-browser clients use a personal API key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Endpoints marked “Session or API key” accept either; endpoints marked “Session only” (saved searches, subscriptions) accept only the cookie, so a leaked key cannot manage credentials. “Moderator” endpoints additionally require the moderator role.

## What is not here

This reference covers every endpoint you can call. A handful are deliberately left out because calling them directly is meaningless: the Gmail and calendar consent redirects (`/me/gmail/connect`, `/me/calendar/connect`, and their callbacks), which only a browser can complete; the Telegram bot webhook; the browser-tool websocket relay; the sitemap-cursor helpers behind `/sitemap.xml`; and the `/og/*.png` social-preview cards, which render an image rather than answer with JSON.

Managing API keys (`POST`, `GET` and `DELETE` on `/me/api-keys`) is not documented here, because no API client can call it. Those endpoints accept only the browser session cookie, and additionally require a freshly proven identity — a password re-entry or a sign-in-provider check — that a script has no way to supply. Create and revoke keys in your account instead, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys); the plaintext token is shown exactly once, at creation, so store it then.

The `/jobs/{slug}/fit` endpoints are pre-rename aliases of `/jobs/{slug}/match-analysis` and hit the same handlers. They still work, so existing clients do not break — use the match-analysis paths in new code.

Most of this API is also a CLI. If you are writing an agent rather than an integration, `freehire` covers the same surface with less ceremony — search, tracking, the inbox and CV tailoring — over one API key.

## External vs internal endpoints

This reference covers endpoints that require the browser’s own session cookie — including moderator-only and browser-extension-only endpoints. None of them accept a personal API key, so an external client or agent cannot call them. For the endpoints a key (or no auth at all) can reach, see [freehire.me/docs/api](https://freehire.me/docs/api).

## Filtering jobs



Except where noted below, these parameters apply to `GET /jobs/search` and `GET /jobs/facets`. Combine any of them with full-text `q`.



- Pass multiple values as a comma-separated list to OR them: `skills=go,rust` matches either. Repeating the param (`skills=go&skills=rust`) also works.

- Add `<param>_mode=and` to require all selected values: `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and` matches both.

- Add `<param>_exclude=<value>` to exclude matches: `company_type_exclude=outstaff` drops outstaff jobs.

- Different facets are ANDed together; numeric and boolean filters are ANDed too. The geography facets are the one exception — see below.

- Geography is a single OR group: `regions`, `countries`, `metros` and `cities` widen each other instead of narrowing. `regions=eu&countries=IT` means "in Europe **or** in Italy", so it returns everything `regions=eu` alone would. To search one country, drop the region: `countries=IT`. The four name a single concept — *where* — so picking two places reads as "either", which is what makes `regions=eu&countries=BR` ("Europe or Brazil") useful. There is no AND to switch on: `_mode=and` does not apply to geography.

- Use `regions=none` to match jobs with no resolved geography (an empty region set); it ORs with real region values and supports `_exclude` like any region.

- A param no filter reads is ignored rather than refused — so old links and saved searches keep working — and comes back in `meta.ignored_params`, with `did_you_mean` when it is only the singular of a real facet. Check it: a dropped filter otherwise looks like a genuinely broad result. At most 10 are listed per response. The same report rides on `/jobs/facets`, `/market/coverage` and `/companies`, which answer `{"data": ...}` and grow a `meta` block only when there is something to warn about. `/companies` filters on its own vocabulary, so a jobs facet sent there is reported as ignored.



### Facets



Every facet below supports repeat-OR, `_mode=and`, and `_exclude` as described above.



| Param | Filter | Values |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `collections` | Collection | yc, techstars, a16z-portfolio, a16z-speedrun, sequoia, accel, greylock, usv, bond, lightspeed, index-ventures, softbank-vision-fund, founders-fund, european, ai, mag7, bigtech, unicorn, fortune500, eastern-roots, indian-roots, ai-native, uk-skilled-worker-sponsor, nl-recognised-sponsor, us-h1b-sponsor, ca-lmia-employer, ie-permit-employer, dk-fast-track-company |

| `regions` | Region | global, north_america, latam, eu, uk, mena, africa, apac, cis, none |

| `work_mode` | Work format | remote, hybrid, onsite |

| `category` | Specialization | software_engineering, backend, frontend, fullstack, mobile, devops, sre, network_engineering, it_support, data_engineering, data_science, data_analytics, ml_ai, ai_engineering, qa, security, hardware, embedded, blockchain, architecture, design, creative, engineering_design, industrial_engineering, occupational_safety, product, project_management, healthcare, skilled_trades, retail, hospitality, logistics, education, personal_services, administration, social_services, science, manufacturing, public_safety, marketing, sales, support, business_analysis, solutions_engineering, developer_relations, technical_writing, recruiting, hr, finance, legal, operations, customer_success, other. The retired value management is still accepted and answered as role_type=people_manager |

| `ai_archetype` | AI Specialization | rag_app_builder, agent_builder, cloud_ml_platform_engineer, ml_trainer_researcher, fullstack_ai_engineer, devops_infra_engineer |

| `seniority` | Seniority | intern, junior, middle, senior, lead, staff, principal, c_level |

| `role_type` | Role type | people_manager — the title names a people-management role. One value only: carrying nothing means no management marker was found, NOT that the posting is individual-contributor work, so role_type_exclude means "no marker", not "IC" |

| `skills` | Skills | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `domains` | Industry | fintech, crypto, ecommerce, gambling, gamedev, media, travel, healthcare, edtech, govtech, devtools, cybersecurity, ai, hrtech, adtech, proptech, logistics, mobility, climatetech, other |

| `company_type` | Company type | product, startup, outsource, outstaff, agency, inhouse, government |

| `countries` | Countries | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `cities` | City | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values. Recognized dictionary aliases such as München and Köln resolve to their canonical city names. |

| `metros` | Metro area | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `relocation` | Relocation | not_supported, supported, required |

| `employment_type` | Employment | full_time, part_time, contract, internship, fellowship |

| `engagement` | Contract terms | ir35_outside, ir35_inside, w2, 1099, c2c, contract_to_hire, b2b, uop, umowa_zlecenie, umowa_o_dzielo, clt, pj, tk, gph, samozanyaty, ip, freiberuflich, arbeitnehmerueberlassung, zzp, auto_entrepreneur, portage_salarial, autonomo, monotributo — employee or own business, in each market's own term (UK IR35, US W-2/1099/C2C, Polish B2B and umowy, Brazilian CLT/PJ, Russian ТК/ГПХ/самозанятость/ИП, German, Dutch, French, Spanish and Argentine freelance statuses), as the title, the description or a source's own contract-type field states it; a posting offering several carries each, one that does not say carries none. Separate from employment_type |

| `english_level` | English | none, a1, a2, b1, b2, c1, c2, native |

| `posting_language` | Job language | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `reality` | Posting reality | fresh, stale, likely-evergreen |

| `salary_currency` | Currency | USD, EUR, GBP, RUB |

| `perks` | Perks mentioned | generous_pto, four_day_week, 401k_match, parental_leave, retirement_plan, tuition_reimbursement, unlimited_pto, health_insurance, mental_health, learning_budget, home_office_stipend, sabbatical, sign_on_bonus — matched from the description; a posting without one does not mention it, which is not the same as not offering it |

| `equity` | Equity | salary_and_equity, equity_only, not_stated — not_stated means none was read, not that the job offers no equity |

| `company_slug` | Company | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `source_type` | Source type | ats, company, aggregator, social |

| `clearance_levels` | Clearance level | none, confidential, secret, top_secret, ts_sci, public_trust, interim, other. none = no detected clearance requirement (the same postings as requires_clearance=false); other = a non-US scheme (UK SC/DV, AU NV1, NATO) or a clearance stated with no level; interim is stated beside a level, not instead of one |

| `source` | Source | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `company_size` | Company size | 1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-500, 501-1000, 1000+ |

| `education_level` | Education level | none, bachelor, master, phd |

| `salary_period` | Salary period | year, month, day, hour |



### Numeric & boolean filters



| Param | Filter | Values |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `visa_sponsorship` | Visa sponsorship | true, false |

| `requires_clearance` | Security clearance required | true, false |

| `via_recruiter` | Posting says a recruiter publishes it for a client | true — the description says so; false — every posting not marked, including recruiter posts that never say so |

| `former_employers` | Hiring again: companies you have worked at and left | true — signed in only, read from your experience bank; a name that does not resolve to exactly one company is left out. Anonymous, it is reported in meta.ignored_params. `/jobs/facets` never applies this filter, so its counts ignore it even for signed-in callers |

| `watchlist` | Your watchlist: companies you follow | true — signed in only; an empty watchlist matches nothing. Anonymous, it is reported in meta.ignored_params. Kept in a saved search, so `watchlist=true` is the alert for new postings at the companies you follow. `/jobs/facets` never applies this filter, so its counts ignore it |

| `salary_min` | Minimum salary | integer — jobs whose minimum salary is at least this (pair with salary_currency) |

| `salary_max` | Maximum salary | integer — jobs whose maximum salary is at most this (pair with salary_currency) |

| `experience_years_min` | Minimum experience | integer — jobs requiring at least this many years |

| `experience_years_max` | Maximum experience | integer — jobs requiring at most this many years, the same figure experience_years_min bounds from below. Use 0 for jobs stating no prior experience is required. Either bound excludes jobs that state no requirement at all, unless experience_include_unspecified is set |

| `experience_include_unspecified` | Include unstated experience | true — with either experience bound, also keep the jobs that state no experience requirement (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without a bound |

| `experience_only_seniority_unspecified` | Experience only without a level | true — apply either experience bound only to the jobs that carry no seniority level; a job with a level passes the bound whatever it states. With seniority and seniority_include_unspecified this reads "one of these levels, or no level and within the bound". Has no effect without a bound |

| `seniority_include_unspecified` | Include unstated seniority | true — with seniority, also keep the jobs that carry no seniority level (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without an included seniority |

| `posted_within_days` | Posted within | integer — jobs whose SOURCE states a posting date in the last N days. Some boards restate that date on every crawl, so a job open for months can satisfy a narrow bound here; open_within_days is the one that cannot be rewritten from outside |

| `open_within_days` | Open within | integer — jobs first recorded by freehire in the last N days, i.e. how long the posting has been in the catalogue regardless of the date its source states. Independent of posted_within_days; both may be set and they narrow together |

| `apply_questions_max` | Application questions | integer ≥ 0 — jobs whose application form requires at most N questions beyond name, contact details and CV (3 = the "short form" filter). Jobs with no form freehire could read are excluded: unknown is not short |



### Recipes



- **Senior Go, remote, in the CIS region** — `q=go&seniority=senior&work_mode=remote&regions=cis`

- **Backend roles, freshest first, in Germany** — `category=backend&countries=DE&sort=posted_at&order=desc`

- **One country only — no region param, or it widens back out** — `countries=IT&employment_type=contract`

- **Must use both Go and Rust** — `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and`

- **Exclude outstaff companies** — `company_type_exclude=outstaff`

- **At least $100k, with visa sponsorship** — `salary_currency=USD&salary_min=100000&visa_sponsorship=true`

- **Excluding jobs that need a security clearance** — `clearance_levels=none`

- **Jobs stating Secret or Top Secret clearance** — `clearance_levels=secret,top_secret`

- **Only jobs that need a security clearance** — `requires_clearance=true`

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Public, unauthenticated reads. Jobs are returned in one wire shape (addressed by `public_slug`, never an internal id) shared by the list, detail, company, and search responses. Closed postings are excluded from lists and search and served only by the detail endpoint.

tags.name: Company feedback
tags.description: Signed-in users leave a 1–5 star rating plus category and text about a company, shown under their site-wide pseudonymous persona (never a user id). Reads are public; writes are cookie-only. A reader can report a specific review, and a moderator can hide it.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Register/login set the session cookie and return the user. Logout clears it. `me` resolves the caller (cookie or API key). OAuth sign-in is a redirect flow.

tags.name: Tracking
tags.description: Per-user tracking, addressed by the job slug. Writes are idempotent. The response is the interaction record for that job.

tags.name: Assistant
tags.description: The same agent the web app and browser extension chat with, over HTTP: create a conversation, then post messages to it. All routes accept the session cookie or an API key (`autopilot` is cookie-only — see below) and act on a session you own; someone else’s session id answers `404`, same as one that never existed. Turns run one at a time per session — a message sent while one is already running queues rather than running alongside it. `preset` selects which conversation this is: `chat` (default), `profile` (the experience interviewer), `browse` (a browsing session held from the extension’s side panel), `interview` (a mock-interview rehearsal), `debrief` (after a real one) or `apply` (the conversation about one automatic application) — the last three must name the vacancy via `?job=<slug>`, an application you already hold. An application holds one `apply` conversation: asking again returns it with `200` instead of creating a second. A `tailor` session cannot be created here; it is minted by the CV tailoring bootstrap, which knows the CV and vacancy to bind it to.

tags.name: Submissions
tags.description: Any signed-in user can submit a vacancy for moderation and read their own queue. The review actions are moderator-only; approval mints a live job.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Any signed-in user can flag a problem with a live vacancy. Review actions are moderator-only; resolving may soft-close the reported job.

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Votes on jobs and companies, and ghost reports: one person states they applied to a posting and were never answered, feeding the ghost-signal evidence used elsewhere in the API (see the `reality` field on a job). Nothing here reaches a moderator and nothing here closes the job directly.

tags.name: Résumé
tags.description: Your career profile and stored CV, session-only (a browser feature, like saved searches). The profile is a singleton keyed by your session — no id in the path. The verdict and ATS report are read-only sub-resources computed from the profile and CV; résumé storage degrades to `501` when object storage is unconfigured.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Browser conveniences, session-only. A saved search stores a canonical filter query string; a subscription turns one into a recurring digest (Telegram, email, or your own webhook). Each operation is owner-scoped — a non-owned id is a 404.

tags.name: Community
tags.description: The lighter per-user surfaces: a vote on a job or company, the account-level notification rule (gates the saved-job apply reminder and both lifecycle nudges), and the public discussion threads. Votes and notification settings take a key; posting to a thread is browser-owned.

tags.name: Referrals
tags.description: Two sides of the same marketplace: an employee offers to refer into the company they work at (proof required, moderated), and a candidate asks one of that company's approved referrers for an intro. A candidate never sees who the referrer is, and a referrer sees the candidate's CV only through a short-lived view. Moderation of offers is moderator-gated.

tags.name: Talent Network
tags.description: A public, anonymised catalogue of candidates who opted into being found. Membership is a single toggle on `users`, distinct from `user_profiles`; a member is addressed by a minted handle, never by their account id or username. Every string a public response carries is a value a dictionary resolved, a number or a date — never text copied from a CV — so no name, employer, institution or free-text field appears anywhere in it.

tags.name: CV
tags.description: Your CVs, and the tailoring flow that reframes one toward a single vacancy. Authoring is browser-owned — create, update and delete are session-only — while reading a CV, patching it, and rendering the PDF also accept an API key, because that is the half a tailoring agent drives. Every CV is owner-scoped: an id you do not own is a 404, not a 403.

tags.name: Experience
tags.description: The durable record a CV is built from: employments, and the evidence atoms under them. Every atom carries who asserted it — you, or a model that inferred it — and only your own assertions may be written into a CV. Reading accepts an API key; editing is session-only.

post.summary: Confirm the address with the mailed code.
Send (or resend) a six-digit email verification code.
post.description:
Mails a fresh code to the caller’s own address, never a body field. Returns
`202 Accepted`. `409` if the address is already confirmed.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

get.description: 404 when checkout is unconfigured or the price is not offered. Cookie session only.
404 when there is no subscription to manage. Cookie session only.

post.summary: Re-read your own store subscription now.
post.description:
For a mobile client that has just completed an App Store or Google Play purchase. The
purchase finishes on the device before the provider’s webhook reaches us, and if that
delivery is lost the provider stops retrying after 80 minutes — so without this route a
paid subscriber can be left looking at a paywall. It names nobody: the account is the
session’s, and a user id in the request is ignored. Absent entirely where the store
provider is unconfigured. `status` is `synced` when the plan was written, or
`no_subscription` when RevenueCat holds nothing for this account; a 503 means the
provider could not be reached and the hourly reconciler will finish the job.

get.description: 404 when the account has no subscription. Cookie session only.

post.summary: Create or overwrite your feedback in one category on a company.
post.description:
One entry per (user, category): posting again in the same `feedback_type` overwrites
your existing review rather than adding a second one. The response's nested `company`
field is the freshly recomputed rating count/average, so you can update your own view
of the company without a second fetch. `422` on an empty body.

Returns the company's freshly recomputed counters, the same cast/clear shape as the

post.summary: Apply on freehire: the employer receives your CV and answers by email.
post.description:
Needs a verified email. The employer gets the chosen CV as a PDF, the answers, the note
and your address as Reply-To. One application per vacancy: `409` once it was sent (or
while it is being sent), `400` naming the first unanswered or invalid question, `403`
unverified, `410` closed, `429` past the daily limit, `502` when delivery failed —
applying again retries it.

post.description: A failure to store or send never surfaces as an error.

post.summary: Drive your own browser to fill an application form.
post.description:
Runs the autofill agent over the browser-tool wire — your extension on one end, the
agent on the other, routed strictly within your own channel. Requires the extension to
be connected, and authenticates only as the extension itself — a session cookie or an
API key gets a 403, since this call writes into whatever form your browser has open,
not just reads it.

get.description:
The tailored copy scored against the base CV it came from, with template, page margins
and typography held identical so the difference reflects content alone — the base is a
copy rendered with the tailored copy’s formatting, never the stored base itself.
Recomputed per request, never stored. `available: false` (with `reason`, no `delta`)
when rendering is unavailable rather than an error. `409` when the CV is not a tailored
copy, has no base CV to compare against, or its vacancy no longer exists.

post.summary: Open the agent conversation for a base CV.
post.description:
Returns the assistant conversation bound to one of your base CVs, creating it on first
use. It is the tailoring workspace's agent without a vacancy: it edits this general CV
through the same evidence-gated tools. Opening it is free and needs no paid plan; each
message still passes the assistant's paid gate. 409 for a tailored copy (use the tailor
session), 404 when the id is not yours.
Drafts the letter (the paid gate runs before this); 402 when the allowance is spent.

post.summary: Copy a base CV.

(copy)". Only a base can be duplicated: 409 for a tailored copy, 404 when the id is not

get.summary: How well a tailored CV matches the vacancy it was written for.
get.description:
Deterministic and free — no model call, unlike the AI match analysis. Scored off the
CV’s rendered PDF text layer against the vacancy alone (no base-CV comparison, unlike
the ATS delta), so it is cheap enough to refresh after every saved edit.
`available: false` when nothing about the vacancy could be matched automatically, or
rendering failed. `409` when the CV is not a tailored copy or its vacancy no longer
exists.

post.summary: Rebuild one CV from your current seed.
post.description:
Replaces this CV's content from the current seed (experience bank first, your résumé's
own extract for what the bank doesn't track). Works on a tailored copy or on a base,
and touches only that CV: refreshing a tailored copy no longer rewrites any base, and
refreshing a base — the editor's "Update from my CV", which replaces hand edits —
leaves its copies alone. Keeps the same id and agent session; preserves template and
typography. 409 when there is no usable seed. Upload alone does not do this — this is
the explicit apply.

get.summary: The edit history of this CV, newest first.
get.description:
Each entry names what changed and where (`paths`), not the edit itself — the operations
carry your own prior text and stay server-side. `undoable` is false for an entry with
nothing to reverse (e.g. the CV’s own creation); `reverted` marks an entry already
undone rather than removing it from the feed.

entry is simply skipped.

One entry per link the PDF carries (header links, project links). Clicks you made on
your own CV are excluded from the counts; `bot_clicks` is tallied separately rather
than folded in. `distinct_visitors` is omitted — not zero — on a deployment with no

unrecognized URL falls back to a generic scrape; pasted text is stored as a private,
unlisted job. Returns the slug the tailor workspace should open — an existing job, or a
freshly created private one. `404` for an unknown `job_slug`, `422` for a URL nothing
could read.

token.description:
The Expo push token minted by the device. (e.g.
`ExponentPushToken[xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx]`)

PushTokenTestResult.description: What a self-test send did per registered device.

approve.description: True approves the referrer; false rejects the offer.

block_domain.description: Also blocks the URL's host and rejects every other pending submission on it.

company.description: The company's fresh counters, set only on the answer to a write.

ReportedCompanyFeedback.description: A review with what a moderator triages by.

SavedSearch.description: A named filter snapshot. `query` is the canonical search query string the SPA replays.

query.description: Empty is the valid "show all" snapshot.

SavedSearchCreate.description: An empty name is refused with a 400, like an out-of-range one.

SavedSearchList.description: The saved searches, most recently updated first.

SavedSearchUpdate.description: A partial update: an absent or null field is kept; an empty query is a real "show all".

authorized_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the candidate may work in.

privacy_consent.description: A standing agreement to an employer form's privacy terms; false asks each time.

ScreeningAnswers.description: Answers an application form asks for, saved once and reused. Each field is optional.

authorized_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the candidate may work in.

privacy_consent.description: A standing agreement to an employer form's privacy terms; false asks each time.

clear.description: Field names to clear. An unknown name is a 400.

change_pct.description: Percent change from the first to the latest week; null without two weeks to compare.

SkillPulse.description: How demand for one of the caller's skills moved.

job_slug.description: The minted vacancy's slug; on an approved submission in the caller's own list only.

Submission.description: A submission as the API shows it.

Subscription.description: One alert on a saved search. `saved_search_name` is sent on the list only.

helpful.description: Whether the conversation helped. A later vote replaces an earlier one.

biggest_challenges.description:
Any of `recruiter_contact`, `job_fit`, `remote_flexible`, `working_abroad`,
`visa_sponsorship`, `technical_interviews`, `english`, `first_job`, `just_starting`,
`other`. `just_starting` stands alone. Replaces the stored list. (e.g.
`["technical_interviews"]`)

biggest_challenge_note.description: Kept only while `other` is among the challenges.

current_income_amount.description: What you earn today, in the currency and period below. (e.g. `5000`)

SurveyResponses.description: The onboarding survey. Each field is optional.

TalentCard.description: The anonymised card: only what a dictionary can vouch for.

TalentEducation.description: One education entry: the degree level a dictionary resolved, and the year.

talent_handle.description: The handle in the member's public URL, once they have one.

listed.description: Whether the catalogue shows the member right now.

TalentNetworkVisibility.description: The caller's own place in the Talent Network.

TalentRole.description: One role of a work history, with everything nameable removed.

ThreadStatus.description: A thread is open until a moderator closes it.

ThreadSubjectType.description: The author is the persona handle, "AI" for a system reply or "[deleted]" once the account is gone.

names.description: Company names or slugs, one per entry. An empty list is refused with a 400.

unmatched.description: Entries that did not resolve to exactly one company, as typed.

max.description: How many companies one list may hold.

CookieSession.name: hire_token
CookieSession.description: Browser session cookie set on sign-in (HttpOnly, same-origin).

PersonalApiKey.description: Personal API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
